baseline.title: Baseline, endogenous signalling: what the body and the day do to the systems with no substance taken
baseline.source: ChatGPT's addition (outside AI), kept: the nervous system runs continuously; exercise, sleep loss, pain, fear, hunger and social experience all shift it. Mechanisms are textbook (exercise raises noradrenaline and endorphins; sleep loss raises adenosine and lowers prefrontal control; pain raises noradrenaline and engages the opioid system; fear is the noradrenaline and cortisol response; hunger raises orexin and ghrelin-driven drive). Sizes are placeholders. NEU-BASE

pk.title: Pharmacokinetics: how a dose becomes a concentration over time (one-compartment model)
pk.source: Standard one-compartment kinetics: C(t) rises with absorption (first-order, half-time ta) and falls by elimination (first-order with half-life t1/2, or zero-order for alcohol at about 0.015 g/dL per hour, Widmark). Alcohol: Widmark factor 0.68 men, 0.55 women; peak 30 to 90 minutes, slower with food (availability 66 to 71% after a meal). Caffeine half-life 3 to 6 hours; nicotine about 2 hours; theobromine 7 to 12 hours; morphine (laudanum) 2 to 4 hours; quinine (bark) 8 to 14 hours; mercury and lead accumulate over weeks to years. NEU-PK, NEU-ALC, NEU-CAF

receptor.title: Receptor dynamics: occupancy, tolerance, dependence, withdrawal (the four clocks)
receptor.source: Occupancy by a saturating function of concentration (Hill, n = 1); fast desensitisation in minutes and slow downregulation over days to weeks (tolerance), with recovery days to weeks after the drug stops (NEU-TOL: CB1 binding back to normal at 7 to 14 days; beta-receptor numbers 16 days; opioid desensitisation reverses in an hour, tolerance slowly). Withdrawal is the rebound of an adapted system without the drug: alcohol 6 to 24 h onset, seizures 24 to 48 h, delirium tremens 48 to 72 h in 3 to 5% with high untreated mortality (NEU-AW); opioids onset 6 to 12 h, peak 1 to 3 days, 5 to 10 days (NEU-OW); caffeine headache 12 to 24 h; nicotine hours.
rows: how much the substance moves each system now
effect_s = potency_s x occupancy, occupancy = C / (C + EC50) ; tone_s = baseline_s + sum over substances of effect_s x sensitivity_s
the system's sensitivity falling under repeated exposure, so the same dose does less
sensitivity_s -= k_tol x mean occupancy over the day, floor 0.3; recovers toward 1.0 at the system's recovery time constant when exposure stops
days to weeks to build (alcohol 2 to 3 weeks of daily drinking for marked tolerance; opioids 1 to 2 weeks; caffeine days), days to weeks to lose
the adapted system now needs the substance to sit at its normal tone (the baseline has shifted the other way)
dependence_s = clamp(1 - sensitivity_s, 0, 1) x exposure days / 14; counts as a need the character acts on (craving: the reward circuit's habit learning and the PSYCHOLOGY push)
the rebound when the substance leaves an adapted system: tone swings opposite to the drug

withdrawal_s = dependence_s x (1 - occupancy) x rebound_s(t), rebound rising from the drug's last elimination to a peak then fading on the recovery constant; alcohol: gaba under, glutamate over (tremor, sweats, fits at 24 to 48 h, delirium at 48 to 72 h if dependence over 0.7, death roll 10% per day of delirium untreated); opioid: opioid under (pain, cramps, gooseflesh, vomiting, no sleep; rarely fatal); caffeine: adenosine over (headache, sleepiness for 1 to 2 days); nicotine: acetylcholine and dopamine under (irritability, craving, days)
hours to days; craving for weeks to months

circuits.title: Functional circuits: from system tones to outputs the rest of the family reads
circuits.source: A functional network, not neurons: each circuit reads the tones that drive it and emits one output on a 0 to 2 scale (1 = normal). The assignment of systems to circuits is textbook neuroscience simplified; the weights are the keeper's placeholders. Receptor activity is not behaviour (ChatGPT's caution, kept): every output is handed to an existing meter or attribute, never to a personality. NEU-CIRC

interactions.title: Several substances at once, and substances on a shifted baseline
interactions.source: Shared systems add at the tone level, not as separate penalties (ChatGPT's requirement, kept); where two depressants hit breathing the human data show a synergistic fall (oxycodone -28% ventilation, +19% more with 1 g/L ethanol, Anesthesiology 2017; NEU-INT). The combination rule is the keeper's.
rows: tone_s = baseline_s + sum over substances (potency x occupancy x sensitivity_s); each circuit then reads the summed tones once. No substance carries a penalty of its own
rum and laudanum both raise gaba and opioid; the arousal circuit falls once, by the sum
respiratory drive = product form: (1 - 0.6 opioidEffect) x (1 - 0.3 gabaEffect) x (1 - 0.2 alcoholEffect), then x0.8 if two or more depressants are over 0.3 occupancy
